steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Latin has six cases: nominative, vocative, accusative, genitive, dative, and ablative. Each case signals a different grammatical function. | Key Fact: Nominative: subject of the verb and complement after verbs like sum (e.g. puella currit — the girl runs; puella est Regina — the girl is queen). | Key Fact: Vocative: used for direct address (e.g. O puella! — O girl!). It is usually identical to the nominative except in second declension masculine singular (e.g. Marce, not Marcus). | Key Fact: Accusative: direct object of a transitive verb, and object of many prepositions (e.g. puellam video — I see the girl; ad villam — to the villa).
